title: SIU clears Windsor police of wrongdoing in shooting death of a man at the Beer Store
article: Ontario's police watchdog has cleared two Windsor police officers of wrongdoing in the shooting death of a Windsor man nearly a year ago.
Police shot and killed Jason West, 57, at the Beer Store on Goyeau Street in Windsor's downtown on Sept. 6, 2024. West died in hospital.
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said on Monday that there were "no reasonable grounds" to believe officers committed an offence.
Police received 911 reports about a man in possession of knives who had been behaving erratically.

The man was highly agitated and paranoid in an interaction with a group of people, according to the SIU report, and had threatened to stab an employee at the nearby Food Basics. He had also reportedly been involved in an altercation where someone was stabbed.
The two officers confronted the man as he was about to enter the Beer Store, the report says. West was in possession of two knives at the time.
Officers repeatedly told West to drop the weapons, the report says. They used a conducted energy weapon, or Taser, twice inside the store but he continued to give chase.

He repeatedly told officers, "Kill me. Kill me," the report says. At one point during the pursuit, an officer shot West after cutting him off as he tried to reach the store's exit. Despite additional gunfire from the other officer, West left the store.
The officers followed West outside and again told him to drop his weapon. West yelled that he wanted officers to kill him, the SIU report says. One of the officers fired his weapon three times.

SIU director Joseph Martino wrote in the report that there was evidence that West was in close range of the officers with knives on him, and given what officers knew prior to their arrival, they would have been concerned that the weapons could be used against them.
Martino said he's satisfied that the officers' use of force was "reasonable" and that they had no other option.

"Though the evidence indicates [West] was not himself on the day in question, he remained a danger given the knives in his possession and his level of agitation," he said. "The officers had cause to intervene in the interests of public safety and they did so in a manner commensurate with the exigent circumstances of the moment."
Following the shooting, a friend of West's set up a small memorial with stones, flowers, a feather and tobacco in front of the Beer Store.
Steven Mull, who goes by Shaman Stirs the Fire, said West was Indigenous and a survivor of the Sixties Scoop. The pair became close friends and briefly lived together.
"I felt so sad. It's like losing your best friend," Mull told CBC News last year.
Matt Johnson, director of programs and services at the Downtown Mission, said West was a "wonderful" person with a great spirit and a great heart, who was also very sick.
"He had struggled with mental illness and substance use for a long, long time, but he was a wonderful dude with a really good heart who always made you laugh," he said at the time.
